category_title: At-risk dyscalculic pupils with core deficits in representing and processing numerosity
minimal_context: The student is working one-on-one with a tutor to count the total number of pips on a mathematics domino card.
dialogue:
TUTOR: We are going to look at some mathematics domino cards today. Can you count out loud for me first?

STUDENT: One, two, three... nine.

TUTOR: Thank you. Now, look at this domino card. Please count the pips from the left side.

STUDENT: (Concentrates on the task and speaks aloud) One, two, three, four, five.

TUTOR: How many pips are there on the domino card?

STUDENT: (Looks around and pauses for a while before starting to count verbally again) One, two, three, four, five... five.

options.A: Challenge the student to see if he gets the same answer by counting the pips from right to left and vice versa.
options.B: Terminate the demands and remove the domino card materials from the student for 10 seconds during the session.
options.C: Deliver verbal statements or gestures (e.g., high five, thumbs up) indicating approval beyond simple acknowledgment during the activity.
options.D: Reassure the student by saying that it is OK, accompanied by physically backing off from the counting activity.
